title: Geopolitical Daily
email_subject: Riyadh hit again as Trump weighs US strikes
preheader: Twelve killed and 309 wounded in the third missile attack on the airport this week.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Sunday, October 11, 2026 — the 2 stories that matter most today, plus 3 updates on stories you're following and 5 quick items from around the world.

stories.story_title: Riyadh airport strike kills 12 as Trump weighs a US role
stories.why_important: A missile hit the passenger terminal at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on Saturday. It killed 12 people from 11 countries and wounded more than 300, the third attack on the airport this week. The Saudi-led coalition blames Yemen's Houthis and promises a decisive response. President Trump says he is weighing a US role.
stories.what_overlooked: Nobody outside the coalition has confirmed who fired the missile. The claim that Houthis did it comes only from Saudi and coalition statements. Riyadh is preparing to host major energy and investment conferences.
stories.prediction: A coalition strike inside Yemen within 72 hours, or a US announcement of direct support, would show whether this widens into a US-backed campaign.

stories.story_title: Trump calls for Ukraine to replace Zelensky as US warns Kyiv on strikes in Russia
stories.why_important: Trump told reporters Ukraine should get a new president who can make a deal. He blamed Zelensky for high US diesel prices. The US warned Kyiv that strikes inside Russia could cost it shared intelligence. That weakens Ukraine's position one day after Washington lifted sanctions on Russian diesel.
stories.what_overlooked: No Ukrainian official has backed the change Trump wants. Ukraine has no elections while martial law remains in force, so there is no legal route to that change.
stories.prediction: Whether Kyiv limits its long-range strikes inside Russia within 72 hours, which would show it takes the threat to shared intelligence seriously.

quick_hits.text: A rights group says an RSF drone strike killed 41 displaced people, including children, near Sudan's border with Ethiopia.
A flash flood on Nepal's Budhi Gandaki river forced villagers to evacuate and damaged homes and infrastructure, with recovery work under way.
Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas postponed legislative and presidential elections to September 11, 2027, blaming Israeli obstacles and the security situation.
The US Justice Department opened an antitrust investigation into ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox News and NBC News for halting coverage of Trump's public events.
Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia killed 20 people, including three children, a day after the US lifted sanctions on Russian diesel.

big_number.context: Aftershocks recorded in Panama after Friday's 7.7-magnitude earthquake, the strongest at magnitude 5.8, as the government declared a state of emergency.
